chapters.title: Final Project: A Multithreaded Web Server

concepts.definition: Rust source is compiled ahead of time into a program; `rustc main.rs` produces an executable. The compiler checks the program before it can run.
concepts.name: Compiling with `rustc`

concepts.definition: `fn main() { }` is where every executable program starts. Function bodies are inside `{ }`. Statements end with `;`.
concepts.name: The `main` function

concepts.definition: `println!` prints text and a newline; `print!` prints without the newline. Placeholders: `{}` with arguments, or a variable name inline: `{name}`. `{{` and `}}` print literal braces.
concepts.name: Printing with `println!` and `print!`

concepts.definition: A name followed by `!` is a macro call, not a function call. Macros can take a variable number of arguments.
concepts.name: Macros vs functions

concepts.definition: `cargo new`, `cargo build`, `cargo run`, `cargo check`; the `src/main.rs` layout; `target/` holds build output.
concepts.name: Cargo projects

concepts.definition: The manifest: `[package]` (name, version, edition) and `[dependencies]`.
concepts.name: `Cargo.toml`

concepts.definition: `let x = 5;` creates a variable. Variables are immutable by default. Deepened in L3.1.
concepts.name: `let` bindings

concepts.definition: `let mut x = 5;` lets the value change. Deepened in L3.1.
concepts.name: Mutable variables

concepts.definition: `std::io::stdin().read_line(&mut buf)` appends a line (including the newline) to a `String`.
concepts.name: Reading a line of input

concepts.definition: `String::new()` makes an empty string; `String::from("hi")` and `"hi".to_string()` make one from text. Deepened in L4.1 and L8.3.
concepts.name: Creating a `String`

concepts.definition: An operation that can fail returns `Result`; `.expect("msg")` gives the value or stops the program with the message. Deepened in L9.3.
concepts.name: `.expect()` on a `Result`

concepts.definition: `use std::io;` brings a name into scope so it can be used without its full path. Deepened in L7.4.
concepts.name: `use` for standard library items

concepts.definition: Adding `rand = "0.10"` under `[dependencies]` in `Cargo.toml`; Cargo fetches and builds it (in the app, crates are bundled). Semantic versioning basics; `Cargo.lock`.
concepts.name: Depending on a crate

concepts.definition: `rand::rng().random_range(1..=100)` picks a random number in an inclusive range.
concepts.name: Random numbers with `rand`

concepts.definition: `a.cmp(&b)` returns `Ordering::Less`, `Equal` or `Greater` (from `std::cmp::Ordering`).
concepts.name: Comparing with `cmp` and `Ordering`

concepts.definition: `match value { pattern => expr, ... }` runs the first arm whose pattern fits. Patterns here: enum variants such as `Ordering::Less`, literals, `Ok(x)`/`Err(_)`, and `_`. Deepened in L6.3.
concepts.name: A first look at `match`

concepts.definition: `s.trim().parse::<u32>()` or `let n: u32 = s.trim().parse()...` turns text into a number. It returns a `Result` because the text may not be a number.
concepts.name: Parsing text into numbers

concepts.definition: `let guess: u32 = guess.trim().parse()...` declares a new variable with the same name, possibly of a different type. Deepened in L3.2.
concepts.name: Shadowing

concepts.definition: `loop { }` repeats forever until `break`; `continue` skips to the next iteration. Deepened in L3.8.
concepts.name: `loop`, `break` and `continue`

concepts.definition: Assigning twice to a variable without `mut` is a compile error (E0384). Immutability prevents accidental changes.
concepts.name: Immutability by default

concepts.definition: `const MAX_POINTS: u32 = 100_000;` must have a type, is always immutable, can be declared at module level, and must be a constant expression. Named in `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
concepts.name: Constants

concepts.definition: `i8`–`i128`, `u8`–`u128`, `isize`, `usize`; default `i32`. Literal forms: `1_000`, `0xff`, `0o77`, `0b1010`, `b'A'`, suffixes like `5u8`. Ranges of each type, e.g. `u8` is 0–255.
concepts.name: Integer types

concepts.definition: In debug builds overflow panics; in release builds it wraps. Explicit handling: `wrapping_*`, `saturating_*`, `overflowing_*`, and `checked_*` (returns `Option`, used from Chapter 6).
concepts.name: Integer overflow

concepts.definition: `f64` (default) and `f32`; float literals need a dot; comparing floats with `==` is risky; `.abs()`, `.sqrt()`, `.powi()`, `.round()`, `.floor()`, `.ceil()`.
concepts.name: Floating-point types

concepts.definition: `+ - * / %`; integer division truncates toward zero; `%` keeps the sign of the left side; `+=` and friends; dividing an integer by zero panics. `.pow()`, `.abs()`, `.min()`, `.max()` on integers.
concepts.name: Numeric operations

concepts.definition: `bool` with `true`/`false`; `&&`, `||` (short-circuit), `!`; comparisons `== != < > <= >=` produce `bool`.
concepts.name: Booleans

concepts.definition: `char` is a 4-byte Unicode scalar value, written with single quotes: `'z'`, `'é'`, `'😻'`. Methods: `is_alphabetic`, `is_numeric`, `is_ascii_digit`, `is_whitespace`, `is_uppercase`, `to_ascii_uppercase`, `to_ascii_lowercase`; `c as u32`; `(b'a' + 2) as char`.
concepts.name: Characters

concepts.definition: `x as f64`, `c as u32`, `n as u8` (truncates), float to int truncates and saturates.
concepts.name: Casting with `as`

concepts.definition: The compiler infers types; annotations (`let x: u64 = 5;`) are needed when it can't, e.g. for `parse`.
concepts.name: Type annotations and inference

concepts.definition: `{:.2}` (precision), `{:5}` / `{:<5}` / `{:>5}` / `{:^5}` (width and alignment), `{:05}` (zero padding), `{:+}`, `{:b}`, `{:x}`, `{:e}`; and `format!` to build a `String` the same way. *(course addition)*
concepts.name: Format specifiers

concepts.definition: `(i32, f64, char)`; access with `.0`, `.1`; destructure with `let (a, b) = t;`; the unit type `()`. Functions can return several values as a tuple.
concepts.name: Tuples

concepts.definition: Fixed length, one type: `[i32; 5]`, `[0; 10]`; index with `a[i]` (`usize`); out-of-bounds index panics at run time; `.len()`.
concepts.name: Arrays

concepts.definition: `fn name() { }`; `snake_case` names; functions can be defined in any order.
concepts.name: Defining and calling functions

concepts.definition: Every parameter must have a type: `fn f(x: i32, label: char)`.
concepts.name: Parameters

concepts.definition: `-> Type`; the last expression without a `;` is the return value; `return` returns early. Adding `;` to the last line returns `()` instead (error E0308).
concepts.name: Return values

concepts.definition: Statements do something and produce no value (`let`); expressions produce a value. A `{ }` block is an expression whose value is its last expression.
concepts.name: Statements and expressions

concepts.definition: `//` line comments; `/* */` block comments. Doc comments come in Chapter 14.
concepts.name: Comments

concepts.definition: The condition must be a `bool` (no truthy numbers).
concepts.name: `if`, `else if`, `else`

concepts.definition: `let x = if c { 5 } else { 6 };`; both branches must have the same type.
concepts.name: `if` as an expression

concepts.definition: `break value` returns a value from `loop`; loop labels `'outer: loop { break 'outer; }`. Builds on `loop.intro`.
concepts.name: `loop` with values and labels

concepts.definition: Repeat while a condition is true.
concepts.name: `while` loops

concepts.definition: `for i in 0..n`, `for i in 1..=n`, `for i in (0..n).rev()`, `.step_by(k)`.
concepts.name: `for` over ranges

concepts.definition: `for x in arr` (copies of elements) and `for x in &arr`; preferred over index loops.
concepts.name: `for` over an array

concepts.definition: Fixed-size values live on the stack; growable data lives on the heap behind a pointer.
concepts.name: Stack and heap

concepts.definition: Each value has one owner; there is one owner at a time; when the owner goes out of scope the value is dropped.
concepts.name: Ownership rules and scope

concepts.definition: A literal `"hi"` is a fixed `&str` built into the program; a `String` is growable heap text. `push_str`, `push`, `len`, `is_empty`.
concepts.name: `String` vs string literals

concepts.definition: Assigning or passing a heap-owning value moves ownership; the old variable can't be used (E0382).
concepts.name: Moves

concepts.definition: `.clone()` deep-copies heap data; it has a cost, so use it on purpose.
concepts.name: `clone`

concepts.definition: Integers, floats, `bool`, `char`, and tuples/arrays of `Copy` types are copied, not moved.
concepts.name: `Copy` types

concepts.definition: Passing a `String` to a function moves it; passing an `i32` copies it.
concepts.name: Passing ownership to functions

concepts.definition: Returning a value moves ownership to the caller; "take and give back" with tuples.
concepts.name: Returning ownership

concepts.definition: `&s` borrows without taking ownership; the function can read but not change.
concepts.name: Shared references `&T`

concepts.definition: `&mut s` borrows with permission to change; the variable itself must be `mut`; dereference with `*r` for `Copy` values.
concepts.name: Mutable references `&mut T`

concepts.definition: At any time, either one `&mut` or any number of `&`; a reference's use ends at its last use (non-lexical lifetimes). Errors E0499, E0502, E0506.
concepts.name: The borrowing rules

concepts.definition: You can't return a reference to a local value (E0106); return the owned value instead.
concepts.name: No dangling references

concepts.definition: `&s[a..b]`, `&s[..b]`, `&s[a..]`, `&s[..]`; indices are **byte** positions; slicing inside a multi-byte character panics.
concepts.name: String slices

concepts.definition: Write `fn f(s: &str)` so it accepts both `&String` (via deref coercion) and literals.
concepts.name: `&str` parameters

concepts.definition: `&a[1..3]` has type `&[i32]`; `fn f(xs: &[i32])` accepts any slice of `i32`.
concepts.name: Array slices

concepts.definition: `for c in s.chars()`, `for b in s.bytes()`, `for (i, c) in s.char_indices()`, `for (i, &b) in s.as_bytes().iter().enumerate()`, `for w in s.split_whitespace()`. Loop use only; iterator chaining comes in Chapter 13.
concepts.name: Looping over text

concepts.definition: `len` (bytes), `is_empty`, `trim`, `to_uppercase`, `to_lowercase`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `chars().count()` (characters), `chars().rev()` in a `for` loop, `repeat`.
concepts.name: Common `&str` methods

concepts.definition: `struct User { name: String, age: u32 }`; `PascalCase` type names.
concepts.name: Defining structs

concepts.definition: Create with all fields; read with `u.name`; the whole instance must be `mut` to change a field.
concepts.name: Creating and using instances

concepts.definition: `User { name, age }` when variables share the field names.
concepts.name: Field init shorthand

concepts.definition: Fields usually own their data (`String`, not `&str`); references in fields need lifetimes (Chapter 10).
concepts.name: Owned data in struct fields

concepts.definition: `User { name: n, ..other }`; moves non-`Copy` fields out of `other`.
concepts.name: Struct update syntax

concepts.definition: `struct Point(i32, i32);` with `.0`, `.1`; different tuple structs are different types even with the same fields (newtypes).
concepts.name: Tuple structs

concepts.definition: `struct AlwaysEqual;` — a type with no data.
concepts.name: Unit-like structs

concepts.definition: Debug output with `{:?}` and `{:#?}`; `dbg!` prints to stderr with file and line, and returns ownership.
concepts.name: `#[derive(Debug)]` and debug printing

concepts.definition: `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]`: what each gives. `PartialEq` allows `==` and `assert_eq!`. *(course addition, from Appendix C)*
concepts.name: Deriving common traits

concepts.definition: `impl Rect { fn area(&self) -> u32 }`; call with `r.area()`; automatic referencing.
concepts.name: Methods with `&self`

concepts.definition: Read, change, or consume the instance.
concepts.name: `&self`, `&mut self`, `self`

concepts.definition: `fn can_hold(&self, other: &Rect) -> bool`.
concepts.name: Methods with more parameters

concepts.definition: Functions in `impl` without `self`, called with `Type::name()`; constructors such as `new`; `Self` names the type.
concepts.name: Associated functions and `Self`

concepts.definition: A type can have several `impl` blocks.
concepts.name: Multiple `impl` blocks

concepts.definition: `enum Direction { North, South }`; variants are namespaced: `Direction::North`.
concepts.name: Defining enums

concepts.definition: `Move { x: i32, y: i32 }`, `Write(String)`, `Quit`: each variant can hold different data.
concepts.name: Variants with data

concepts.definition: `impl Message { fn call(&self) }`.
concepts.name: Methods on enums

concepts.definition: `Some(value)` or `None` instead of null; you must handle `None` before using the value; `.is_some()`, `.is_none()`, `.unwrap_or(default)`.
concepts.name: `Option<T>`

concepts.definition: `slice.get(i)`, `.first()`, `.last()`, `s.find(pat)`, `s.chars().next()`, `c.to_digit(10)`, `char::from_digit`, `checked_add`/`checked_sub`/`checked_mul`/`checked_div`. *(course addition)*
concepts.name: Standard methods that return `Option`

concepts.definition: One arm per variant; arms are expressions with the same type.
concepts.name: `match` on enums

concepts.definition: `Coin::Quarter(state) =>` binds the inner value.
concepts.name: Binding values in patterns

concepts.definition: Every possible value must be covered, or the code doesn't compile (E0004).
concepts.name: Exhaustiveness

concepts.definition: `other =>` binds the value; `_ =>` ignores it; `_ => ()` does nothing.
concepts.name: Catch-all arms

concepts.definition: `1 | 2 =>`, `'a'..='z' =>`, `90..=100 =>`. *(course addition here; covered fully in L19.3)*
concepts.name: `|` and range patterns

concepts.definition: `if let Some(x) = opt { } else { }` for one pattern.
concepts.name: `if let`

concepts.definition: `let Some(x) = opt else { return ...; };` keeps the happy path unindented; the `else` must diverge.
concepts.name: `let...else`

concepts.definition: Binary and library crates; `src/main.rs` and `src/lib.rs` as crate roots; a package can have both.
concepts.name: Packages and crates

concepts.definition: `mod name { }` groups items; modules nest into a tree under `crate`.
concepts.name: Defining modules

concepts.definition: Items are private to their parent module by default; `pub` makes them visible; children can see their ancestors' private items. Error E0603.
concepts.name: Privacy

concepts.definition: Absolute `crate::a::b` and relative `a::b`, `self::`, `super::`.
concepts.name: Paths

concepts.definition: A `pub struct`'s fields stay private unless each is `pub` (so it needs a constructor); a `pub enum`'s variants are all public.
concepts.name: Public structs and enums

concepts.definition: `use crate::a::b;` then `b::f()`; bring functions' parent modules in, but types themselves. `use` only applies in its own scope.
concepts.name: `use` and idiomatic paths

concepts.definition: `use std::io::Result as IoResult;`.
concepts.name: Renaming with `as`

concepts.definition: `pub use` makes an item available at a new path.
concepts.name: Re-exporting with `pub use`

concepts.definition: `use std::{cmp::Ordering, io};`, `use std::io::{self, Write};`, `use std::collections::*;`.
concepts.name: Nested paths and glob imports

concepts.definition: `mod garden;` loads `src/garden.rs` (or `src/garden/mod.rs`); submodules in `src/garden/vegetables.rs`.
concepts.name: Modules in separate files

concepts.definition: `Vec::new()`, `vec![1, 2, 3]`, `vec![0; n]`, `push`; the vector must be `mut` to change.
concepts.name: Creating and updating vectors

concepts.definition: `v[i]` panics when out of range; `v.get(i)` returns `Option<&T>`.
concepts.name: Reading elements

concepts.definition: Holding `&v[0]` while calling `v.push` is an error (E0502), because pushing may move the buffer.
concepts.name: Borrowing rules with vectors

concepts.definition: `for x in &v`, `for x in &mut v { *x += 1 }`, `for x in v` (consumes).
concepts.name: Iterating over vectors

concepts.definition: An enum lets one vector hold values of different kinds.
concepts.name: Vectors of enums

concepts.definition: `len`, `is_empty`, `pop`, `insert`, `remove`, `swap`, `contains`, `sort`, `sort_unstable`, `dedup`, `reverse`, `extend_from_slice`, `truncate`, `clear`, `iter().sum()` / `max()` / `min()` in their simplest form, `join` on `Vec<String>`/`&[&str]`. Methods that take closures come in Chapter 13.
concepts.name: Common vector methods

concepts.definition: `String::new`, `String::from`, `to_string`, `String::with_capacity`.
concepts.name: Creating strings

concepts.definition: `push_str`, `push`, `+` (takes ownership of the left side, borrows the right), `format!`, `insert`, `pop`, `clear`.
concepts.name: Updating strings

concepts.definition: No integer indexing (E0277); `len` counts bytes; three views: bytes, `char`s, grapheme clusters (not in std).
concepts.name: Strings are UTF-8

concepts.definition: Byte ranges must land on character boundaries or the program panics; `is_char_boundary`, `char_indices` to find safe positions.
concepts.name: Slicing strings safely

concepts.definition: `chars()`, `bytes()`, `char_indices()`, `lines()`, `split(pat)`, `split_whitespace()`, `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `strip_prefix` (returns `Option`).
concepts.name: Iterating strings

concepts.definition: `use std::collections::HashMap;`, `HashMap::new()`, `insert`.
concepts.name: Creating hash maps

concepts.definition: `get(&k)` returns `Option<&V>`; `.copied().unwrap_or(0)`; `contains_key`; `remove`; `len`.
concepts.name: Reading from hash maps

concepts.definition: `for (k, v) in &map`; the order is **arbitrary**, so sort keys before producing ordered output.
concepts.name: Iterating hash maps

concepts.definition: Inserting a `String` key or value moves it into the map; `Copy` values are copied.
concepts.name: Ownership in hash maps

concepts.definition: Overwrite with `insert`; insert only if missing; update from the old value.
concepts.name: Updating values

concepts.definition: `*map.entry(k).or_insert(0) += 1`; `or_insert_with(Vec::new)`; `or_default()`.
concepts.name: The `entry` API

concepts.definition: Unique values: `insert` returns `bool`, `contains`, `remove`, `len`; iteration order is arbitrary. *(course addition)*
concepts.name: `HashSet`

concepts.definition: Stops the program with a message; also triggered by bugs such as out-of-bounds indexing; `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`.
concepts.name: `panic!`

concepts.definition: `Ok(value)` or `Err(error)`; handle with `match`. Returning `Result` from your own functions.
concepts.name: `Result<T, E>`

concepts.definition: `match e.kind() { ErrorKind::NotFound => ..., other => ... }`; parse errors (`ParseIntError`).
concepts.name: Matching on error kinds

concepts.definition: Shortcuts that panic on `Err`/`None`. Prefer `expect` with a message; from Chapter 9 on, graded code may not use `unwrap()` unless a problem says so.
concepts.name: `unwrap` and `expect`

concepts.definition: Returning the `Err` to the caller instead of handling it.
concepts.name: Propagating errors

concepts.definition: `let x = f()?;` returns early with the error; converts error types with `From`; only in functions that return `Result` (or `Option`). Error E0277 when used in a function returning `()`.
concepts.name: The `?` operator

concepts.definition: `?` on an `Option` returns `None` early. Mixing `?` on `Option` and `Result` in one function doesn't work.
concepts.name: `?` with `Option`

concepts.definition: `opt.ok_or(err)`, `res.ok()`, `unwrap_or`, `unwrap_or_default`. Closure-taking forms (`map_err`, `ok_or_else`) come in Chapter 13. *(course addition)*
concepts.name: Converting between `Option` and `Result`

concepts.definition: `fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>`; `Box<dyn Error>` as "any error" (fully explained in Chapter 18).
concepts.name: `main` returning `Result`

concepts.definition: An `enum` of error cases, deriving `Debug` and `PartialEq` so tests can compare; carrying data in variants. *(course addition)*
concepts.name: Custom error types

concepts.definition: Panic for broken invariants and bugs; `Result` for expected failures such as bad input.
concepts.name: When to panic vs return `Result`

concepts.definition: A type whose constructor checks its value (e.g. `Guess::new` for 1–100), with a private field and a getter.
concepts.name: Types that validate

concepts.definition: `fn largest<T: PartialOrd>(list: &[T]) -> &T`; extracting duplicated code into a function first.
concepts.name: Generic functions

concepts.definition: `struct Point<T> { x: T, y: T }`, `Point<T, U>`.
concepts.name: Generic structs

concepts.definition: `Option<T>` and `Result<T, E>` are generic enums; defining your own.
concepts.name: Generic enums

concepts.definition: `impl<T> Point<T>`, `impl Point<f32>`, methods with their own generic parameters.
concepts.name: Generic methods and specialised `impl`s

concepts.definition: Generic code is copied for each concrete type at compile time, so it has no run-time cost.
concepts.name: Monomorphization

concepts.definition: `trait Summary { fn summarize(&self) -> String; }`.
concepts.name: Defining traits

concepts.definition: `impl Summary for Tweet { }`; calling trait methods needs the trait in scope.
concepts.name: Implementing traits

concepts.definition: You can implement a trait for a type only if the trait or the type is local to your crate (E0117).
concepts.name: The orphan rule

concepts.definition: Methods with a body in the trait; implementors can override; defaults can call required methods.
concepts.name: Default method implementations

concepts.definition: `fn notify(item: &impl Summary)`.
concepts.name: `impl Trait` parameters

concepts.definition: `fn f<T: Summary + Display>(x: &T)`; `where` clauses; multiple bounds.
concepts.name: Trait bounds and `where`

concepts.definition: `fn make() -> impl Summary`; only one concrete type can be returned.
concepts.name: Returning `impl Trait`

concepts.definition: `impl<T: Display + PartialOrd> Pair<T> { fn cmp_display(&self) }`; `impl<T: Display> ToString for T`.
concepts.name: Conditional and blanket impls

concepts.definition: `impl fmt::Display` (so `{}` and `to_string` work), `PartialOrd`/`Ord` with `derive` or by hand, `From` for conversions. *(course addition)*
concepts.name: Implementing common std traits

concepts.definition: The borrow checker compares scopes so a reference never outlives its data (E0597).
concepts.name: Why lifetimes exist

concepts.definition: `fn longest<'a>(x: &'a str, y: &'a str) -> &'a str`; the result lives as long as the shorter input. Error E0106 without one.
concepts.name: Lifetime annotations in functions

concepts.definition: `struct Excerpt<'a> { part: &'a str }`; the struct can't outlive the borrowed data.
concepts.name: Lifetimes in structs

concepts.definition: The three rules that let you omit annotations, including `&self` methods.
concepts.name: Lifetime elision

concepts.definition: `impl<'a> Excerpt<'a>`; returning references tied to `self`.
concepts.name: Lifetimes in methods

concepts.definition: String literals are `&'static str`; `'static` bounds; why "add `'static`" is rarely the right fix.
concepts.name: `'static`

concepts.definition: `fn f<'a, T>(x: &'a str, y: &'a str, ann: T) -> &'a str where T: Display`.
concepts.name: Generics, bounds and lifetimes together

concepts.definition: `#[test]`, `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; }`; a test fails when it panics.
concepts.name: Test functions and the test module

concepts.definition: The values compared must implement `PartialEq` and `Debug`; left/right in failure output.
concepts.name: `assert!`, `assert_eq!`, `assert_ne!`

concepts.definition: Extra `format!`-style arguments after the assertion.
concepts.name: Custom failure messages

concepts.definition: Normal cases, edges (empty, one item), boundaries (0, max, off-by-one), Unicode, error paths; one behaviour per test; descriptive names. *(course addition)*
concepts.name: Choosing test cases

concepts.definition: Test that code panics; `expected = "substring"` makes it precise.
concepts.name: `#[should_panic]`

concepts.definition: `fn t() -> Result<(), String>` so `?` can be used; can't combine with `should_panic`.
concepts.name: Tests returning `Result`

concepts.definition: `cargo test name_filter`, `-- --test-threads=1`, `-- --show-output`, `#[ignore]`, `-- --ignored`.
concepts.name: Controlling test runs

concepts.definition: Unit tests live with the code and can test private functions.
concepts.name: Unit tests and private functions

concepts.definition: The `tests/` directory; each file is a separate crate using only the public API; shared helpers in `tests/common/mod.rs`; binary-only crates can't be integration-tested.
concepts.name: Integration tests

concepts.definition: `std::env::args()` yields `String`s, the first being the program name; `.collect::<Vec<String>>()` (collect explained in L13.4).
concepts.name: Command-line arguments

concepts.definition: `fs::read_to_string(path)` returns `Result<String, io::Error>`.
concepts.name: Reading a file
